I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou County best. I know this system, I can manage it with the labor I have, and it matches our water, weather, and local selling channels. I will carry the winter wheat through spring and early summer with moderate fertilizer, a few key irrigations, and pest control only when pressure rises, because my goal is stable grain, not chasing the highest possible yield with the highest cost. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize right away so I do not lose soil moisture or time. For wheat I will use an improved common variety, and for maize I will use hybrid seed because maize hybrids usually give me better stand and yield. I will use rotary tillage before wheat and mostly no-tillage after wheat for maize so I can save time and hold moisture. I will keep inputs practical and familiar, with enough nitrogen to support yield, phosphorus and potassium to keep the soil from falling behind, and irrigation focused on the growth stages that matter most.
